result.title: Physics-Informed One-Step Generation on Long-short flow maps
result.summary: Physics-informed generative models should produce samples that are both data-aligned and physically valid, yet existing methods are often iterative and too slow for practical use. Achieving this with a one-step flow-map model is difficult because both data-distribution and physics-constraint learning are enforced only indirectly through surrogate objectives, making their joint learning fragile for long-range flow maps. We propose \textbf{Physics-Informed Long-Short Flow Maps with Direct Guidance (LSFM-DG)}, which makes direct target computation feasible by decomposing one-step generation into a long flow map for global evolution and a near-terminal short flow map with computable closed-form solutions and physics potentials. As the short flow map shrinks to zero, it provides both direct distributional and physical targets for learning the long flow map. This yields a unified one-step flow-map model that removes Jensen's gap, improves training stability, and achieves stronger data fidelity and physical consistency without distillation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 LSFM-DG，将一步生成分解为负责全局演化的长流映射与近终端、具闭式解的短流映射，由后者为前者提供直接的分布与物理约束目标，实现无需蒸馏的一步生成。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 无直接关联，但其「长-短映射分解＋近终端可计算目标替代间接代理目标」的思路，可能为长程 latent 推理轨迹的直接监督与贡献分配提供启发，可供核查多尺度分解能否迁移。
